title: Harness Engineering: What's Actually New (And What Isn't)
excerpt: Harness engineering is the new name for everything around the model: tools, context, guardrails, telemetry. Carly Richmond, Senior Manager of Developer Advocacy at Elastic, shows what's genuinely new about building agents, and why most of the harness still rests on software engineering fundamentals you already know. What we cover: – What harness engineering is, and how it builds on prompt, context and loop engineering – What's genuinely new: non-determinism, tool calling and models that change under your feet – Why TDD evolves into AI agent evals, and when LLM-as-a-judge is the wrong tool – Writing tool descriptions for agents the way you'd write an OpenAPI spec – Telemetry, guardrails and security for an agent harness Chapters: 00:00:00 - Introduction 00:02:26 - What is harness engineering? 00:04:45 - Prompt vs context vs harness vs loop engineering 00:06:33 - What's genuinely new about building agents 00:09:28 - Incremental changes, pipelines and testing 00:12:09 - From TDD to AI agent evals 00:14:04 - Context engineering and why LLMs get things wrong 00:17:41 - Tools, OpenAPI and agent orchestration 00:21:43 - Observability, security and guardrails for agents 00:28:12 - Key takeaway and audience Q&A Build your software factory, one workflow at a time, with Tessl: https://tessl.co/t5v 🔔 Subscribe for weekly videos on AI-native development Which parts of harness engineering feel new to you, and which feel like the same old fundamentals? title: Automated AI Code Review on GitHub, Set Up in 2 Minutes
excerpt: See Tessl Code Review in action as we review a real pull request from Nuclei, an open-source vulnerability scanner, and uncover issues missed in the original review. In this walkthrough, you'll learn how to: - Connect Tessl Code Review to your GitHub repository in minutes. - Automatically review new pull requests and get actionable, line-level feedback. - Configure reviews to run in comment-only or blocking mode. - Identify bugs, reliability issues and potential performance problems. - Use review feedback in automated workflows to improve code quality before merging. Tessl Code Review can also be integrated into a software factory, where issues are passed back to coding agents for automated fixes and further review.
